GATE TABLE for the default backend 'native_cb' (each row points at the check that decides it):
  correctness vs the legacy compiled graph : D6 - 320 origins (64 committed + 256 surface band),
                                             neighbour passes disabled, 0 mismatches required
  module execution                         : X13/X14/X15/X16/X17 - an added module changes the
                                             output, a no-op does not, an unexecutable one is refused
  concurrency                              : X22 - live terrain on 4 engine worker threads,
                                             streamed voxels == harness voxels, 0 rejected writes
  live streaming                           : X22 (same run) + tools/probe_native_live.gd
  cost                                     : B1/B2/B5/B6 below

  native_cb            harness=2.716 ms/column (cold region 9.117)  cliff(extent1)=52.321 ms/column (19.26x)  engine-native=3.557 ms/column
  graph                harness=0.133 ms/column (cold region 3.846)  cliff(extent1)=n/a (legacy baseline)  engine-native=n/a
  noise2d              harness=0.076 ms/column (cold region 0.444)  cliff(extent1)=n/a (legacy baseline)  engine-native=n/a
  experimental_columns harness=2.755 ms/column (cold region 8.968)  cliff(extent1)=59.240 ms/column (21.50x)  engine-native=n/a

COST VERDICT: the default modular backend costs 20.5x the legacy compiled graph per column
on the HARNESS path (2.716 vs 0.133 ms/column). The graph is a C++ compiled node graph with no
module pipeline at all, so this is the price of scriptability, not a regression: the graph
cannot run a module from user://modules (evidence E2) and is gated behind
allow_legacy_baseline for exactly that reason.

That ratio is large enough to matter on the target device, so it is recorded as a KNOWN
COST DEBT with the measured levers, not waved away:
  * engine-native writes are already ~3.5x cheaper than per-voxel writes (do_box spans);
  * the region field cache means one coarse tile serves 64 columns (cache stats in B1);
  * the remaining harness cost is GDScript module dispatch, which only the engine path (B6)
    and, later, a compiled graph generated FROM the module plan can remove;
  * quality_scaling retraction (T9) is wired: a module with factor <= 0 is skipped.

B6 measures the same backend through the engine's own column path: 3.557 ms/column.

RECOMMENDATION: keep 'native_cb' as the default. It is the only backend that satisfies the
correctness, module-execution, concurrency and live-streaming gates at once; 'experimental_columns'
(the self-hosted column generator, never the extension's MultipassCB) matches it on correctness but
has no engine worker threads and no engine mesher integration, and the two legacy baselines fail
the module-execution gate outright.
